figures.title: Growth-temperature diffraction, PL, TEM and distributions
figures.summary: Panels a–c show diffraction, time-resolved PL and normalized PL for growth at 25, 50 and 100 °C. OAm:OA is 1:3 and washing is 1:20 acetonitrile:toluene. Panels d–f are TEM images with 20 nm bars; the 100 °C inset labels d(002) = 6.38 Å. Panels g–i report mean dimensions of 7.6 ± 2.4, 9.5 ± 1.6 and 10.4 ± 1.1 nm, with histogram FWHM values 5.7, 3.7 and 2.7 nm. The ± statistic is undefined. The 25 °C diffraction marks PbI2 and δ-FAPbI3 alongside α-phase assignments.

intuition.title: Ligand, purification and phase interpretations
intuition.summary: The authors relate ligand balance and washing conditions to precursor availability, passivation, dissolution and nonradiative recombination. Their temperature-dependent phase and emission model uses cited bulk reference cells. These explanations remain author interpretations, separate from measured occupancies, atomic coordinates, device performance or independently reproduced mechanisms.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Ligand mechanism interpretation
intuition.summary: The authors associate excess OAm with protonated OAm+ replacing FA+ and disrupting the lattice, insufficient OA with reduced FA-oleate formation, and excess OA with hindered growth and dissolution in washing solvent. These are mechanistic explanations, not measured occupancies, solution structures or reaction stoichiometries.

general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Amine coordination
general_background.summary: An amine nitrogen can donate electron density to suitable solution species or surface sites. Donation from the nitrogen lone pair and competition with other ligands can change precursor speciation and surface association.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
